findings.F1: The test's result is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: in the explore half, the 61 cases (46 case-days) gain +4.6 % over the coin's mean 3-day return, with a day-pooled t of 1.84. Step 5's full measure is +1.8 % with t 1.36 on 115 case-days.
findings.F2: The effect is graded by the swing-scaled 3-day rise inside the rising agitated profile.
findings.F3: The effect lives in the profile. Equally large swing-scaled rises outside rising agitated bars, the ones the vetoes send to chop, are followed by −0.4 % over 3 days (126 cases, t −0.49).
findings.F4: The 3-day horizon is where the effect shows best.
findings.F5: The effect is positive on every coin, but each coin has few cases, so its strength cannot be told from noise on this data.
findings.F6: The move is about the size that real ideas show, and it is above the cost of a trade. Its strength is 0.034 of the usual move, its total move per case is +0.83 % against a 0.26 % trade cost, and its unusual move is t 0.49. The test is short of cases, not short of an effect on the predicted side.

ideas.name: scaled burst continues, more coins
ideas.idea: In a rising, agitated market, a coin whose 3-day return is large against its usual daily swing (the standard deviation of its daily returns over the last 30 days) keeps rising over the next 3 days, and the larger that swing-scaled rise, the larger the further rise.
ideas.consequence: Staged forced buying (squeezed faders, underweight holders and swing-sized traders) makes a short rise that stands out against the coin's own swing continue, more so the larger it is in swing units.
